answer: A farm that captures 189 seats hence pays for 189 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the pigment quorum in the spiral ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the pearl history makes public each cut. Jurors whose votes correlate above 33% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. That is 8 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
